# 2 Baruch Chapter 56 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** The Cloud and Waters Vision
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 56:7 — individual moral responsibility vs Adam

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "each-of-us has-been-the-Adam-of-his-own-soul" |
| LOGOS | "each of us has been the Adam of his own soul" |
| PNEUMA | "each of us has been his own Adam" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** SOPHIA adopted LOGOS. The Syriac idiom 'Adam of his own soul' is a key theological formulation in 2 Baruch expressing individual accountability; LOGOS preserves the exact phrase while PNEUMA's paraphrase loses the term 'Adam'.

---

## 56:4 — effects of the fall — catalog

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | "the-begetting-of-children was-brought-about, the-passion-of-parents was-produced" |
| LOGOS | "the begetting of children was brought about, the passion of parents was produced" |
| PNEUMA | "childbearing came into existence; the suffering of parents began" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** SOPHIA adopted LOGOS. 'The passion of parents' (Syriac: regtha d-ahhe) refers to parental anxiety/suffering; PNEUMA's 'suffering' is acceptable but loses the specific word 'passion' which has theological resonance.
